reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it actively promotes OneCoin as a financial opportunity using urgent recruitment appeals, large income claims, and promises of financial freedom while directing viewers to enroll and recruit others. The presentation ties earnings to multi-level sales teams and matching bonuses, and also promotes paid educational packages whose tokens are sent to a mining operation and coins whose value is expected to appreciate. The speaker presents these mechanisms as an opportunity viewers should not miss rather than as a warning or investigation.

citations.quote: recruit as many people as you can share with as many people as you can
you purchased one of our educational packages and we will give you tokens, and those tokens you send to the mining operation
as we grow and do the splits and everything in manage the price a week be at fifty euros 200 euros
get more than one point sign-up start enrolling people

opening.argument: The presentation itself distinguishes projections from guarantees. Its growth slide labels the figures as an “Optimistic Scenario” and “Base Scenario,” and expressly states that the price chart is based solely on projections and is not a financial forecast. The speaker likewise characterizes the higher-value scenario as “just a prediction” and “a type of financial forecast.” That risk-qualified presentation is more consistent with conditional market commentary than deceptive certainty. The claims invite viewers to assess possible outcomes, while the material identifies the assumptions as projections rather than established returns.

citations.quote: this is just a prediction this is now a type of financial forecast

rebuttal.rebuttal: The call to enroll does make the presentation promotional, but promotion alone does not establish that the claims are presented as guaranteed. The cited recruitment language shows an invitation to participate, while the forecast slide expressly limits its price scenarios to projections. The evidence therefore supports conditional investment commentary, not necessarily deceptive certainty.

citations.quote: get more than one point sign-up start enrolling people

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The disclaimer is narrow and does not neutralize the broader sales pitch. The same presentation urges viewers to seize the opportunity, predicts prices of “fifty euros 200 euros,” and presents projected wealth as a reason to act. Calling a claim a forecast does not show that the underlying opportunity or compensation structure is reliable.

citations.quote: seize the day, and make the most of it to create financial freedom for you and your family
as we grow and do the splits and everything in manage the price a week be at fifty euros 200 euros

opening.argument: The material can be understood as an educational walkthrough of digital-currency concepts and company operations. It promises to explain “what cryptocurrency is,” describes algorithms, mining, wallets and exchanges, and identifies education as a central offering. The slides also present a step-by-step business introduction system and an ADC system explaining automation, duplication and creation. Those features support a tutorial or demonstration reading: the speaker is showing how the proposed system works and explaining terminology, rather than merely making an unsupported accusation or hidden transaction.

citations.quote: our other promises to educate you on digital currencies
I told you one of the promises, we're going to talk about what cryptocurrency is

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats every explanation of compensation as solicitation, but an explanation can also be instructional. The presentation explicitly calls its content education and explains operational concepts such as wallets, mining and exchanges. Its business-system discussion shows how the system is intended to function; it does not by itself prove that the video’s primary purpose is deceptive recruitment.

citations.quote: we're gonna show you our sample 3-step business introduction system
The mining operation is soft enough equations to get you your five thousand coins.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The educational framing is inseparable from the sales pitch. The tutorial explains how to purchase packages, obtain tokens and recruit through the system, then directs viewers to enroll. Explaining mechanics does not make the promotion neutral, especially where the promised education is packaged with access to coins and compensation opportunities.

citations.quote: you purchased one of our educational packages and we will give you tokens
get more than one point sign-up start enrolling people

opening.argument: The described activity includes recognizable commerce and financial-service functions: an e-wallet, payments, a debit card, and an exchange where coins can be bought and sold. The presentation describes coins being used to send money or pay retailers and describes converting them through an exchange. It does not show the speaker requesting a credential, taking a deposit directly, or guaranteeing a return. The existence of referral commissions and an exchange can therefore be read as ordinary business promotion and customer acquisition, without enough evidence that the mechanism itself is fraudulent.

citations.quote: you can do that with your e-wallet
You can sell your coins on the exchange

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited compensation language describes commissions and team volume, but commissions can accompany ordinary referral or sales programs. The presentation also describes direct sales, an exchange and payment functions. Without evidence of a requested credential, a guaranteed return, or a specific fraudulent transaction, the record supports a commercial opportunity more directly than it proves a scam.

citations.quote: you get paid 10% on the 60,000 euros
You can sell your coins on the exchange

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is not merely a retail referral program. The presentation ties packages and tokens to mining, commissions to sales-team volume, and bonuses to multiple generations. It explicitly encourages recruiting and says tokens enable access to more coins. The absence of a credential request or an explicit guarantee does not remove the central recruitment-and-purchase mechanism.
